items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: But he had Tut Soper, and Tut, again, had done something in the band that they wanted him to leave yesterday, for some reason.

ctx.x: Same story. So this was the Chicago scene that I was involved in. And -- which brings me to the time I finally looked at my hands and said, what am I doing, and I started teaching.

And then work, whatever I could and then what saved me was in 1959, Bob Scobey came to town and called me. Now, I had bad recollections of Scobey from the Lou Waters band. So when he called me, I was visiting my daughter. And I says, no, I don't read that good to read your charts. I'm not interested in joining a band. But he had Tut Soper, and Tut, again, had done something in the band that they wanted him to leave yesterday, for some reason. I don't know what he did. I don't blame it on his playing because I…
He can play more like Earl Hines than Earl Hines can. ... piano player I ever played with.
